public_rationale: Marcus said OpenAI had never turned a profit. Credible reports before the post show losses every year with known figures. The Information reported a $540M loss in 2022, double the 2021 loss. The NYT, citing OpenAI's own financial documents, reported an expected loss of about $5B in 2024. In January 2025, Salon said plainly that OpenAI 'hasn't turned a profit.' No source reports a profitable year for OpenAI at any point before May 2025. The claim matches the public record.
limitations: OpenAI is private. The evidence is press reporting of company documents, not audited filings.
Full figures for the early nonprofit years (2015-2020) and for 2023 were not checked year by year.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI has never turned a profit.

statement.excerpt: Here, fully modern and way beyond parody, is Sam Altman — whose company, mind you, has never turned a profit — promising to use AI to capture the value of a large fraction of the entire universe (the earth’s light cone, to be exact).

from_speaker: stated as of the post date, 2025-05-17
our_interpretation: Plain reading: from its founding in 2015 up to May 2025, OpenAI never reported or was credibly reported to have an annual net profit.
Because OpenAI is private, credible press reports of its financials are the best evidence available before the post. They count as estimates.
criteria.support_condition: Credible reports show OpenAI ran net losses in the years with known figures (for example 2022 and 2024), and no credible source reports any profitable year before May 2025.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A credible filing or report shows OpenAI had a net profit in any year (or a profitable full reporting period) before May 17, 2025.
